key_insight: LLM-guided feature discovery outperforms direct LLM reasoning when ranking candidate protein–ligand poses in the Pyrite benchmark.
engineering_relevance: Combining molecular geometry, interaction data, and physicochemical scores with learned ranking could improve candidate-pose prioritization in drug-discovery workflows.
method: Encode pose geometry, protein–ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores using PyriteRep.
Compare poses directly with PyriteReasoner or generate executable features for logistic regression with PyriteFeaturizer.
Apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to improve open-weight models.
evidence_signal: Across 1,500 pose pairs, PyriteReasoner and PyriteFeaturizer achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, while evaluated expert chemists perform near chance.
watch_item: Benchmark accuracy does not establish generalization to new targets or prospective drug-discovery settings.
paper_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
